notes.2: This question was well answered by many candidates. Candidates seemed to be able to relate the answers to the glasshouse. Some candidates gave incorrect types of sensor, for example ‘growth sensors’.
notes.3: This was a well answered question with most candidates circling the correct features.
notes.4: This topic of expert systems, as previously, was found to be challenging. (a) This question, which was in three parts, asked for three components of an expert system. Many candidates found the question challenging and some left the answer spaces blank. Candidates completed part (iii) better than the other two parts. (b) As with part (a) this part of the question was quite challenging.
notes.7: On the whole, candidates produced good answers for parts (a) and (b) . (a) Most candidates understood which fields were needed for each of the validation rules. Some candidates missed the underscores when writing down the field names. There were fewer candidates in this series that wrote down the content of the table rather than the field name. (b) Most candidates were able to identify ISBN for the answer. (c) Most candidates could gain some credit here by explaining that using an electronic book reduced the amount of physical space that printed books would take up. Some candidates correctly identified that using electronic books could give the user eye strain. As with other ‘describe’ questions, candidates were more successful if they gave reasoned answers. notes.8: Most candidates did well on this question, especially part (b) . (a) This question was a ‘discussion’ question and therefore required the candidates to give detailed answers for and against the use of handprints to enter a building. Most candidates seemed to understand the basics of biometric systems. Correct answers were often about the uniqueness of the handprint and the fact that you do not forget it. Candidates were not as clear on the drawbacks, but there were some good, detailed answers. (b) Most candidates were successful on this part.
notes.9: A range of answers were allowed for this question, including ‘abide by the laws within the country that affect the general use of emails’. Sometimes candidates tended to concentrate on what should be in an email, such as salutations and the message.
notes.13: This question was quite well answered by candidates. Most candidates who answered the question related it to not giving out personal information.
notes.14: This proved a challenging question for candidates to answer. Many candidates could not clearly differentiate between the different types of break, tending to use the names as guides. notes.15: Candidates produced some good answers for this question, particularly for part (c) . (a) Acceptable answers to this part were pen drives or the use of the Cloud. Some candidates stated USB, which is a port on the computer, or via email, but did not expand on this to state it was an attachment. Some candidates answered by stating the work would be printed out. Credit was generally given for stating the method rather than the advantage and disadvantage of its use. The question is a ‘discussion’ question and therefore candidates needed to compare the positives and negatives of using each method with others. (b) Many candidates correctly stated that encryption was the scrambling of data in order to protect it. Some added that it would stop hacking, which it would not do. This is a ‘describe’ question and therefore candidates needed to expand on their answers. (c) This part was well answered by most of the candidates. notes.11a: This question asked candidates to state two ways in which data could be searched for on the Web. Acceptable answers included ‘using a search engine’ or ‘typing in details onto the search bar’. Some candidates wrote about clicking on links or asking a teacher.
notes.11b: This was the more technical part of the question, which asked for the differences between the internet and the Web. Some candidates knew that the internet was a WAN and that the WWW was part of the internet.
notes.12a: This part of the question asked candidates to state and describe two development layers, having been given an example of the other layer. Some candidates were able to write down at least one development layer.
notes.12b: This part asked why tables were used in web pages. Candidates were able to give answers relating to organising the elements on the web page, but some answers lacked detail.
